title: Hierarchical Comments with Underlines or Formatting Shifts
pattern: Differentiating major and minor comment levels using all-caps, underlines, or initial ellipses within a single function body.
why_bad: Increases complexity. This custom visual hierarchy is highly subjective, tedious to maintain, and requires the reader to learn a custom markup standard for a single file.
detection: Inline comments where consecutive blocks shift from uppercase with underlines to lower-case with custom symbols (like `...`).
counterexample: Uniform sentence-case comments; a function complex enough to need an outline is split into well-named helpers instead.
fix: Simplify all comments to use consistent standard layout (regular sentence casing, no custom hierarchies); split the complex function if it requires an outline to read.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("C++ Example of Differentiating Between Major and Minor Comments").
